items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to alcohol training awareness programs
items.lawCode: Amd §§65 & 17, ABC L; amd §260.20, Pen L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A8645

TITLE  OF BILL:   An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in
relation to alcohol training awareness programs

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL: To encourage those who hold  a  license
to  sell  alcoholic  beverages  at  retail and their employees to attend
alcohol training awareness programs in an effort to stem underage drink-
ing and alcohol overconsumption

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS: Section one amends  section  65  of  the
alcoholic beverage control law (ABC law) by adding two new subdivisions,
7  and  8. Subdivision 7 provides that in a proceeding to revoke, cancel
or suspend a license to sell alcoholic beverages at retail where  it  is
alleged that the licensee violated subdivision one or subdivision two of
this section, and the licensee has not had any adjudicated violations of
the  ABC  laws  within  the past five years, if a licensee holds a valid
certificate of completion or a renewal, the civil  penalty  shall  be  a
bond  revocation  only.  Subdivision  8 provides that in a proceeding to
revoke, cancel or suspend a  license  to  sell  alcoholic  beverages  at
retail  where  it is alleged that a licensee violated subdivision one or
subdivision two of this section and the charge is sustained by the state
liquor authority, if the licensee agrees that all of  employees  of  the
licensee shall obtain a valid certificate of completion or renewal with-
in  ninety  days of the finding of such offense and the licensee has not
had any other adjudicated violations of the ABC  laws  within  the  past
five years, the civil penalty shall be reduced by twenty-five percent.

Section two amends the closing paragraph of subdivision 12 of section 17
of  the alcoholic beverage control law, as amended by chapter 549 of the
laws of 2001, by providing  that  alcohol  training  awareness  programs
shall  be  attended  in  person,  through  distance learning methods, or
through an internet based online program.

Section three provides the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION: It is not merely anecdotal that underage  drinking  is  a
problem  throughout  the  country,  including  New  York  State. Alcohol
related injuries and deaths occur at an alarming rate. According to  the
Insurance  Institute  for  Highway Safety, 28% of passengers, age 16-20,
who were fatally injured in motor vehicle accidents in the state in 2007
had a blood alcohol content level of .08 or more.  Non-vehicular alcohol
related accidents and deaths are generally on the rise as well. In 2005,
the monetary cost to New York State, which includes the cost of  medical
care and work loss, was $3.2 billion, according to the Pacific Institute
for  Research and Evaluation; making New York the 38th highest in under-
age drinking related costs in the  country.  Such  figures  do  not,  of
course,  reflect  the immeasurable cost of pain and suffering related to
injuries and death stemming from alcoholic consumption by minors.

Overconsumption by those who are twenty-one years of age or older  nega-
tively  impacts  New York and its residents as well. According to recent

statistics published by the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles,
one third of all vehicular fatalities in the state involved impaired  or
intoxicated drivers and pedestrians.

Alcohol  Training  Awareness  Programs, authorized by the New York State
Liquor Authority (SLA) are currently available to  licensees  and  their
employees.  Such  programs,  however,  are  under-attended. It is widely
acknowledged that attendance at such programs decreases  the  incidences
of  serving alcohol to minors, and helps servers recognize customers who
are visibly intoxicated.

By providing real world  incentives,  this  legislation  will  encourage
those  who  hold  a  license  to sell alcoholic beverages at retail, and
their employees, to attend alcohol training  awareness  programs  in  an
effort to stem underage drinking and alcohol overconsumption.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: This is a new bill.

FISCAL  IMPLICATION:  Reduced  revenues  from  possible  civil penalties
collections, however, his will be more than offset by the savings to the
state in costs associated with alcohol related injuries and deaths.

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it
shall have become a law.

BILL NUMBER:A8645A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in
relation to alcohol training awareness programs; and to amend the penal
law, in relation to unlawfully dealing with a child in the first degree

the ABC laws at the licensed premises where the alleged violation
occurred within the past five years, if a licensee holds a valid certif-

revocation only. Subdivision 8 provides that in a proceeding to revoke,
cancel or suspend a license to sell alcoholic beverages at retail where

shall be attended in person, through distance learning methods, or

an affirmative defense to a prosecution pursuant to subdivision two of

quent to the commencement of the present prosecution, has completed an

their employees, to attend alcohol training awareness programs in an

FISCAL IMPLICATION: Reduced revenues from possible civil penalties

BILL NUMBER:A8645B

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS: Section one amends subdivision 4 of

defense to any proceeding pursuant to subdivision one of section 65 of
the ABC law.

Section two amends subdivision 6 of section 65 of the ABC law, as
amended by chapter 481 of the laws of 1999, by providing that it shall
be an affirmative defense to any proceeding pursuant to section one
hundred eighteen of the ABC law where it is alleged that a person
violated subdivision one of section 65 - selling, delivering or giving
away alcoholic beverages to a person under the age of twenty-one - that
such person reasonably relied on a photographic identification card
presented by the person to whom the alcoholic beverages were sold,
delivered, or given. The liquor authority, in evaluating the applicabil-
ity of such affirmative defense, shall consider any written policy
adopted and implemented by the seller.

sion 7. Paragraph (a) of subdivision 7 provides that in a proceeding

cancel, or suspend a license to sell alcoholic beverages, in which

or two of section 65 and the licensee has not had any adjudicated
violation of the ABC law at the licensed premises where the violation
occurred within the past five years, and the person who committed such
violation held a valid certificate of completion or a renewal from an
alcohol training awareness course, the civil penalty shall be the recov-
ery of the penal sum of the bond on file during the period in which the
violation took place. Paragraph (b) of subdivision 7 provides, alterna-
tively, that at the time of such violation, if the licensee has not had
any adjudicated violations of the ABC law at the licensed premises with-
in the previous five years any civil penalty imposed shall be reduced by
twenty-five percent if the licensee submits written proof that all
employees at the time of the violation who are involved in the sale of
alcoholic beverages have obtained a valid certificate of completion from
an alcohol training awareness program.

Section four amends the closing paragraph of subdivision 12 of section
17 of the ABC law, as amended by chapter 549 of the laws of 2001, by

providing that alcohol training awareness programs shall be attended in
person, through distance learning methods, or through an Internet based
online program.

Section five amends subdivision two of section 260.20 of the penal law
by adding a new third undesignated paragraph which provides that it
shall be an affirmative defense to a prosecution pursuant to subdivision
two of section 260.20 of the penal law - unlawfully dealing with a child
in the first degree - that at the time of the alleged violation, the
defendant had not been convicted of a violation of sections 260.20 or
260.21 of the penal law, within the previous five years and such defend-
ant, subsequent to the commencement of the present prosecution, has
completed an alcohol training awareness program. A reasonable adjourn-
ment of the proceedings may be granted to enable such defendant to
complete the training program.

Section six provides the effective date.

as well. In 2005, the monetary cost to New York State, which includes

the Pacific institute for Research and Evaluation; making New York the

tion by minors.

tively impacts New York and its residents as well. According to recent

employees. Such programs, however, are under-attended. It is widely
acknowledged that attendance at such programs decreases the incidences

are visibly intoxicated.

those who hold a license to sell alcoholic beverages at retail, and
their employees, to attend alcohol training awareness programs in an
effort to stem underage drinking and alcohol overconsumption.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: 2009, passed in the Assembly. Same as
S.5803-A (Klein).

collections, however, this will be more than offset by the savings to

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it
